complexity.explanation: Instantiating a CanvasGradient object executes in constant O(1) time and space by allocating an internal color-ramp table. Geometric rasterization occurs per pixel during fillRect on the GPU/rasterizer.

executionTrace.memoryDetail: Resolves and caches reference to HTMLCanvasElement node in DOM tree.
Initializes 2D graphics state machine and binds to backing render buffer.
Allocates CanvasGradient descriptor tracking focal point (150, 150, r0=0) and outer boundary (150, 150, r1=100).
Appends normalized color tuples (0.0: indigo, 1.0: dark surface) to internal color-ramp buffer.
Binds active fill pointer to gradient; GPU fragment pipeline evaluates concentric color interpolation across 90,000 pixels.

pitfalls.title: Negative Radii Cause Immediate DOMException
pitfalls.description: Supplying negative values for either r0 or r1 causes createRadialGradient to immediately throw an IndexSizeError DOMException and terminates render execution.
pitfalls.badSnippet:
// Unclamped radius calculation crashing at runtime
const gradient = ctx.createRadialGradient(x, y, -10, x, y, 100);
pitfalls.goodSnippet:
// Always clamp radii to non-negative floats
const gradient = ctx.createRadialGradient(x, y, Math.max(0, r0), x, y, Math.max(0, r1));

pitfalls.title: Sub-pixel Blur on High-DPI Displays (Retina / Mobile)
pitfalls.description: Setting canvas dimensions without accounting for window.devicePixelRatio results in an under-sampled bitmap that stretches across physical device pixels, blurring fine gradient ramps.

seniorInterviewTip: Senior graphics interviewers watch whether you understand that createRadialGradient creates two concentric circles with independent centers (x0, y0, r0) and (x1, y1, r1). Offsetting the centers simulates a 3D spherical light source, while keeping them concentric produces a flat 2D glow. Always mention GPU color-stop interpolation overhead when evaluating fill performance.
